summary: Implemented DownloadButton, a reusable ATOM taking `enabled`/`comment` per context.json, plus the useDocumentDownload hook and the getDocumentDownload service call wiring GET /api/v1/contracts/{contractId}/document/download. Wired both into ContractDocumentTab (built by an earlier task, which had explicitly left this endpoint/atom unimplemented and called out T-DOWNLOAD-BUTTON-UI by name): an oversized document renders a disabled Download button with the 'File unavailable' comment beside it (UC8-BR-006), while a corrupted/missing document keeps Download enabled and, on click, calls the download endpoint and surfaces 'This document could not be retrieved. Please contact your administrator.' without altering any other contract fields (UC8-AF-005). A healthy document downloads normally via the same enabled button and endpoint. Matched the dark bordered button + download-icon styling shown in IMG-3's Document tab. Verified with lint (0 warnings), the full vitest suite (19 files / 95 tests passing, incl. 3 new DownloadButton tests and 3 new ContractDocumentTab tests covering all three states), and a production build. Visually verified by standing up a disposable local mock API (not part of the app, removed afterward) and screenshotting /contracts/:id for an enabled, an oversized/disabled, and a corrupted/still-enabled document — all three match the design's button placement, icon, and dark styling; .env.local was restored to its original value afterward.

pr.title: feat(ui-gen): add DownloadButton and wire document download/error states
pr.body: Implements DownloadButton (UC8-AF-005, UC8-BR-006): a reusable Download control with an enabled state that calls the new useDocumentDownload hook (GET /api/v1/contracts/{contractId}/document/download) and a disabled state showing the 'File unavailable' comment. Wires both into ContractDocumentTab, which an earlier task (T-CONTRACT-DETAIL-PAGE-UI) had deliberately left pointing at documentUrl directly and flagged this endpoint/atom as out of its scope. Oversized documents now show a disabled Download button with 'File unavailable'; corrupted/missing documents keep Download enabled but show 'This document could not be retrieved. Please contact your administrator.' on click, without touching any other contract field.

blockers: Inferred two props beyond context.json's literal `enabled`/`comment` contract for DownloadButton: `onClick` (callback to trigger the download) and `isLoading` (disables the button and shows 'Downloading…' while the request is in flight). Neither is listed in context.json's component entry, but the atom is otherwise non-functional without a way to invoke the download — derived from the paired useDocumentDownload hook's `download()`/implicit in-flight state, not invented from scratch.

ContractDocumentTab.jsx (owned by the earlier T-CONTRACT-DETAIL-PAGE-UI task) was modified to replace its placeholder anchor/disabled-button pair with the new DownloadButton + useDocumentDownload. This is not a new screen rewrite — that file's own code comment explicitly named this task (T-DOWNLOAD-BUTTON-UI) as the owner of the download endpoint and atom it was deliberately stubbing out, so completing that stub was treated as this task's job rather than out-of-scope editing of another module's screen.

None of IMG-1..IMG-4 show the disabled/'File unavailable' Download state or the AF-005 corrupted-document error message — only IMG-3 shows a healthy, enabled Download button. The disabled and error-message visuals were built to match this repo's established dark/bordered button language (same family as the existing placeholder in ContractDocumentTab) rather than a specific design reference, since no TARGET DESIGN depicts those states.

Visual verification required a disposable local mock API server (not committed) because this sandbox has no running backend; .env.local was temporarily repointed at it and restored to its original value before finishing, and the mock server/process were torn down.
